issues: At 1x the silhouette reads more as a tiny fish or bug with a trailing tail than as a squid with a distinct mantle and tentacles.
The oversized adjacent eyes dominate the left half, leaving little room for a recognizable robotic body or mine-like casing.
The right-side tentacles merge into a noisy, horizontally striped cluster; the long black tips resemble fins or speed lines.
Several cyan and black pixels around the tentacle roots form awkward one-pixel notches and weakly connected clusters.
The broad white area and pale-blue shading use more interior modeling than typical MM2/MM3 small-enemy sprites, while the mechanical construction remains vague.
The sprite is wider than the intended compact 16–20 px footprint and lacks a clear gathered-versus-thrust tentacle pose.
No visible eye-light housing or other cue supports the red-warning and explosive-mine behavior.
fixes: Compress the sprite to roughly 18x18 px and build it around a clear domed or triangular squid mantle.
Place two smaller eyes inside one black-outlined faceplate rather than using two large separate eye circles.
Replace the right-side striped mass with three or four individually readable tentacles, each made from clean 2–3 px clusters.
Create two animation poses: tentacles tucked tightly beneath or behind the body, then extended in a broad thrust fan.
Use a consistent one-pixel outer contour and remove isolated cyan notches at the tentacle roots.
Limit each hardware sprite region to black plus two body colors and transparency; reserve white or red for the eye modules through palette swapping.
Add a small central seam, rivet, or underside nozzle to make the creature unmistakably robotic and mine-like.
Prepare a warning frame that swaps the eye whites or pupils to red immediately before the explosion.

issues: The large rounded upper body and two square lower pods read more like a submarine or wheeled machine than a compact robot squid.
The right-side appendages are rigid horizontal bars and angular fins; they do not read as flexible tentacles gathering and thrusting.
At 1x, the eyes, body opening, and appendages merge into an unclear cyan-black cluster.
The silhouette is too wide and mechanically scattered for the intended roughly 16x16 to 20x20 compact enemy.
Black outlining is inconsistent: the dome has a heavy top edge, blue areas lose their contour, and the rightmost bars end in blunt black blocks.
Several narrow one-pixel projections and abrupt stair-steps on the right create noisy, weak clusters rather than deliberate Capcom shapes.
White, pale cyan, bright cyan, dark blue, and black appear together in small regions, exceeding the disciplined tile-level palette treatment typical of Mega Man 2-3.
There is no clearly readable eye pair or alternate visual cue suggesting the red warning-flash behavior.
fixes: Compress the design into a compact 16x18 silhouette with one rounded mantle above and three or four tentacles below.
Replace the long right-facing bars with short, thick two- or three-pixel tentacle clusters; make a gathered frame and a separate splayed thrust frame.
Place two simple one-pixel eyes together on the front of the mantle, with a palette-swap frame changing them to red before detonation.
Remove the two square lower pods, which resemble wheels or goggles, and use that space for a single clear face and tentacle root.
Use a consistent one-pixel dark outline around the outer silhouette while reserving interior black for the eyes and one or two structural separations.
Reduce each 8x8 region to black plus two body colors and transparency; use white only as a tightly controlled highlight if the tile palette permits it.
Eliminate isolated tips and long one-pixel lines, rebuilding the appendages as chunky 2x2 and L-shaped clusters.
Give the mantle a simpler Capcom-style highlight: one compact light patch on the upper-left rather than multiple stepped cyan bands.

issues: The true-size footprint is roughly 36x23 pixels, substantially larger and wider than the intended 16x16 to 20x20 enemy.
At 1x the horizontal silhouette reads more like a small fish or rocket than a Blooper-like robot squid; the right-side tentacles resemble speed lines or exhaust.
The two oversized square-ring eyes dominate the body and leave the mantle, mine casing, and tentacle anatomy poorly separated.
The right-side appendages contain long parallel black bars, isolated blue steps, and awkward white blocks that look assembled rather than deliberately clustered.
The mantle uses black, white, pale cyan, bright cyan, and blue across nearby regions, exceeding the simple NES sprite-palette discipline unless built from conspicuous overlay sprites.
The pale diagonal streaks on the mantle create modern glossy rendering rather than the compact, symbolic highlight treatment typical of Mega Man 2-3.
There is no clear visual provision for the warning state: the eye areas are too large and structurally busy for a clean red flash.
fixes: Reduce the design to about 18x18 pixels and make the mantle a compact rounded trapezoid occupying the upper 9-10 rows.
Place two small 2x2 or 2x3 eyes beneath the mantle, with one shared dark brow line; reserve a single eye color slot that can swap to red during the warning frame.
Move the appendages below the body and build three distinct tentacles from clean 2-pixel-wide clusters instead of long horizontal bars.
Create two animation poses: a gathered pose with tentacles tucked into a compact lower cluster and a thrust pose with them extending 2-3 pixels downward or backward.
Use one black outline color, one main body color, and one light color per hardware-sprite region; remove either the pale cyan or bright cyan tier.
Replace the mantle's multiple diagonal streaks with one short 2-3-pixel highlight cluster near the upper-left edge.
Close outline gaps and eliminate the isolated steps around the right and lower-right extremities so every pixel reinforces a readable mass.

issues: The roughly 20x28 px bounding box is too tall for the intended 16x16 to 20x20 enemy scale.
The diagonal silhouette reads more like a rocket, fish, or comet than a Blooper-like squid; the tentacles merge into one pointed striped tail.
The top black projection resembles an antenna and does not clarify the mantle or swimming motion.
The face presents one large rectangular eye or opening rather than a clear pair of eyes that could flash red.
The cyan-and-white checker pattern through the lower-left tail is visually noisy at 1x and lacks the compact cluster control typical of Mega Man 2-3 sprites.
Several areas appear to require black, white, cyan, and dark blue within the same 8x8 region, exceeding a normal NES sprite palette's three opaque colors.
The thick stair-stepped black mass along the lower-right contour makes the outline uneven and visually heavy.
There is no clearly articulated gathered-versus-thrust tentacle pose, so the pulsing swim behavior is not communicated by the design.
fixes: Compress the complete silhouette into a maximum 20x20 box, with a broader rounded mantle and shorter underside tentacles.
Replace the single tapered tail with two or three separated tentacle tips, leaving one-pixel negative-space cuts between them.
Create two animation frames: tentacles tucked tightly under the body, then extended downward or backward for the thrust.
Redesign the face as two compact one-pixel eyes or two 1x2 eye clusters; use a palette-swap frame that changes them to red before detonation.
Limit each 8x8 sprite region to black plus two body colors, removing either white or one blue where all four currently overlap.
Replace the lower checkerboard striping with one solid shadow cluster and one small highlight cluster.
Regularize the right and lower outlines to a consistent one-pixel contour, removing the bulky black staircase near the tail junction.
Remove or reshape the top antenna into a small mantle point or side fin so the silhouette reads immediately as a squid.

issues: The lower-left appendages merge into one striped, pointed mass, reading more like a rocket exhaust or fish tail than gathering squid tentacles.
The body has only one clearly readable eye; the large white facial patch and black square do not establish the described paired flashing eyes.
The black contour becomes 2-4 pixels thick along the right and underside of the body, unlike the controlled one-pixel outlines typical of Mega Man 2-3 enemies.
The diagonal outline and tentacle area contain heavy stair-stepping and cramped cyan-white-blue clusters that become muddy at 1x.
The sprite uses black, white, cyan, and dark blue together in small tile regions, making the NES sprite-palette construction questionable.
The silhouette lacks a clean separation between bulbous head and multiple tentacles, weakening both animation potential and mine-like character.
fixes: Replace the fused pointed tail with three short, individually separated tentacles using one-pixel gaps; create distinct gathered and thrust animation frames.
Use two compact eyes, each one or two pixels wide, and reserve a red palette swap or separate frame for the proximity warning.
Reduce the right and lower black masses to a mostly one-pixel contour, keeping thicker black only at deliberate interior separations.
Simplify the head into a rounder, more symmetrical 10-12 pixel bulb with fewer diagonal staircase changes.
Remove either white or dark blue from crowded 8x8 regions, using black plus two body colours per hardware sprite layer.
Open the negative space around the tentacles and eliminate the alternating diagonal stripe pattern so the appendages remain legible at true size.

issues: At 1x the diagonal silhouette reads more like a tiny rocket, drill, or comet than a floating squid.
The face lacks two clearly separated eyes, so the red-warning behavior has no obvious visual anchor.
The long upper black stalk feels like an antenna and weakens the squid-like mantle silhouette.
The lower-left appendages merge into one narrow, noisy mass instead of reading as tentacles gathering for a thrust.
The outline varies from one to several pixels thick around the right and lower body, unlike the controlled Capcom contouring of MM2/MM3.
Large white and cyan interior shapes form awkward stair-steps and make the body look hollow rather than mechanically constructed.
The sprite is taller than the intended compact 16-20 px footprint and has weak visual balance around its diagonal axis.
fixes: Compress the silhouette into a roughly 18x18 body-and-tentacle footprint.
Remove or shorten the top stalk and shape the upper body as a broad, rounded squid mantle with small side fins.
Place two distinct 1-2 px eyes across the front of the body; reserve a red alternate-frame color for the warning flash.
Separate the lower appendage into three bold tentacles with clean 2-3 px-wide clusters and two animation poses: gathered and thrust outward.
Reduce the heavy right-side and underside black masses to a mostly 1 px contour, using thicker black only at deliberate shadow joins.
Replace the checker-like white/cyan interior with one simple white face plane and one cyan shadow band.
Keep the strong black, cyan, and white palette, but arrange each color into larger, cleaner NES-style clusters.

issues: The large rectangular white eye panel makes the body read more like a helmet or ghost than a floating squid.
The lower cyan mass forms one blunt block instead of distinct tentacles gathered for a swimming thrust.
The right-side appendage is visually detached and resembles an arm or tail rather than part of a radial tentacle arrangement.
The bottom and right contours use heavy, square black masses inconsistent with Mega Man 2-3's economical 1-pixel outlining.
Several staircase transitions around the dome, eye panel, and lower body are lumpy rather than deliberately clustered.
Both eyes are featureless black slots; the described red warning flash is not represented in the shown state.
At 1x, the eye panel remains visible, but the propulsion anatomy and mine-like function are unclear.
The palette is suitably limited, but the broad white area dominates and leaves little room for Capcom-style cyan volume accents.
fixes: Reduce the white eye panel by one pixel around its perimeter and separate the eyes with a cleaner central bridge.
Round the dome with deliberate 2-1 or 2-2 pixel stair steps and keep the exterior outline predominantly one pixel thick.
Split the lower cyan block into three short tentacle tips with one-pixel black gaps; angle the outer tips inward for the gathered pose.
Attach the right-side form directly to the body or replace it with a symmetric side tentacle so it does not appear to float separately.
Remove the solid black bottom-right blocks and restore cyan interior pixels bounded by a clean one-pixel contour.
Give each eye a compact pupil cluster and create an alternate warning frame that swaps the eye interiors to a single NES red.
Add one small cyan highlight cluster near the upper-left dome while keeping each tile within the existing limited palette.
Design a second thrust frame with the tentacles extended downward or backward to make the pulsing swim action readable.

issues: The right-side appendage reads as a fish tail or exhaust plume rather than squid tentacles.
The lower cyan body is a nearly solid block, so the gather-and-thrust tentacle anatomy is not visible.
At 1x the silhouette reads more like a small fish or flying face than a Blooper-like swimming mine.
The white face plate dominates the body and gives it a mask-like, modern mascot appearance rather than a mechanical Capcom construction.
Heavy black clusters at the lower-left edge and around the right appendage make the outline uneven and obscure the body connection.
The limited black, white, and cyan palette is disciplined and NES-plausible, but the sprite lacks a visible mechanical or explosive cue.
fixes: Remove the rear tail shape and place two or three short tentacles beneath the body, separated by 1px black notches.
Create two animation poses: tentacles tucked inward for gathering and extended downward/backward for thrust.
Trim 1px from each side of the white face plate and restore a consistent 1px black shell border around it.
Reduce the lower-left black mass by 1px and simplify the right body contour into cleaner stair-step clusters.
Add one small mechanical seam, fuse, or central mine detail using the existing black and cyan colors.
Make a warning frame that palette-swaps the eye pixels to a bright NES red immediately before detonation.

issues: The right-side appendage reads as a fish tail or cannon rather than gathered squid tentacles.
The lower body is a broad rectangular cyan mass, so the silhouette lacks distinct thrusting tentacle tips.
The oversized white face panel and large square black eyes make the enemy resemble a ghost or mask more than a robotic swimming mine.
The right appendage has bulky stair-steps and a narrow attachment point that feel assembled rather than cleanly articulated.
At 1x, the eye and face contrast survives, but the body action and squid identity collapse into an indistinct dark shape.
There is no visible mine cue or red warning-eye state in the presented design.
The palette is disciplined and NES-plausible, but the nearly equal visual weight of black, white, and cyan produces a harsher, less nuanced Capcom look.
fixes: Replace the right-side tail shape with two or three separated 1-pixel-wide tentacle tips beneath the body.
Narrow the lower cyan mass by 1-2 pixels and carve black gaps between tentacles to establish a squid silhouette at 1x.
Reduce the white face panel by one pixel along its sides and bottom, leaving more cyan shell around it.
Change the square eye holes into smaller mechanical eyes with white resting pixels and a red flash frame for the warning animation.
Clean the right contour into deliberate 1-pixel stair-steps and widen its body connection so it does not look pasted on.
Create two animation poses: tentacles tucked tightly under the shell, then splayed downward/backward for the thrust pulse.
Add one compact mine-like mechanical cue, such as a single top rivet, seam, or side fuse nub, without introducing extra palette noise.

issues: The oversized joined white eye mass dominates the center and feels more like modern cartoon pixel art than an MM2/MM3 robot face.
The lower-right tentacles merge into a broad diagonal shape that reads as a leg or tail rather than gathered squid arms.
The lower-left appendage has an uneven staircase contour and a cramped white tip, weakening the silhouette at 1x.
The body lacks a clear mechanical feature such as a casing seam, rivet, intake, or mine-like trigger.
Black, white, cyan, and dark blue occur close together across the head, making NES sprite-palette separation awkward.
Nothing in this frame suggests the red warning-eye state described for the enemy.
fixes: Reduce each eye by 1 pixel and separate them with a continuous 1-pixel black bridge; square the eye corners into cleaner Capcom-style clusters.
Narrow the lower-right cyan mass and split its tip into two distinct 2- to 3-pixel tentacles with black negative space between them.
Redraw the lower-left tentacle with a simpler two-step contour and remove the cramped white end pixel.
Add one economical mechanical cue on the upper shell, such as a 2-pixel highlight slit or a black casing seam.
Keep each 8x8 region to black plus two active colors where possible; reserve white primarily for the eyes and use cyan or dark blue for the shell.
Create a warning frame that replaces the white eye interiors with a single NES red while preserving the same black eye outlines.

issues: The squid silhouette reads at 1x, but the long, uneven lower-right appendages make the pose look tangled rather than like gathered or thrusting tentacles.
The two eyes are treated inconsistently: the left has a clear pupil while the large right eye appears blank, weakening expression and instant facial readability.
The upper dome and right edge contain heavy black masses instead of the controlled one-pixel contour and compact shadow clusters typical of Mega Man 2-3 enemies.
Several contour stair-steps around the lower-left body and rightmost tentacles are lumpy, with awkward single-pixel turns and near-orphaned tips.
Black, white, cyan, and multiple blues appear together across crowded regions, exceeding the simple three-opaque-color logic expected within many NES sprite tiles.
The design reads more as an organic Blooper than a Capcom robot or swimming mine; it lacks a seam, rivet, casing panel, fuse, or other mechanical cue.
The trailing white appendage merges visually with the eye whites and competes with the face, reducing hierarchy at true size.
fixes: Give both eyes matching one-pixel pupils and reserve a clean alternate red-eye frame for the warning animation.
Shorten the lower-right extensions and organize them into two or three distinct tentacles with clear gathered and thrust animation poses.
Replace the thick top and right black masses with a mostly one-pixel outline, using only small two-pixel black clusters at deep overlaps.
Redraw the lower contour with deliberate 1-1 or 2-1 stair-step rhythms; remove isolated tip pixels and flatten the long horizontal foot-like ending.
Limit each 8x8 region to black plus two body colors, or black, white, and one body color; use separate tiles or palettes only where clearly justified.
Add one compact mechanical identifier, such as a forehead seam, side rivet, or small mine arming light, without increasing the palette.
Keep tentacles blue and reserve white primarily for the eyes so the face remains the strongest focal point.

issues: The oversized white eye masses dominate the body; the right eye lacks a clearly readable pupil, making the expression look unfinished at 1x.
The lower-right tentacle forms a long, irregular white-and-black hook that reads more like a tail or loose debris than a squid tentacle.
The tentacle area has several awkward one-pixel stair-steps and narrow gaps, especially beneath the center and along the right thrusting limb.
The broad black cap across the top and heavy black mass on the right make the outline thicker and less economical than typical MM2/MM3 enemy work.
Black, white, dark blue, and cyan appear together across crowded regions, creating a four-color sprite treatment that would require careful hardware-sprite layering.
The design communicates a squid, but not the mine behavior: there is no visible warning-eye state, explosive cue, or especially mechanical detail.
fixes: Give both eyes matching 2x2 or compact L-shaped black pupils and reserve red for a separate warning-flash frame.
Shorten the lower-right appendage by 2-3 pixels and divide the bottom into three clearly spaced, rounded tentacle tips.
Remove isolated staircase pixels beneath the body and rebuild each tentacle from clean 2-pixel-wide clusters.
Reduce the top black band by one pixel in its center and trim the right-side black mass to a consistent one-pixel contour.
Consolidate each 8x8 region to black plus two shared colors; use either white and cyan or white and dark blue, adding the fourth color only through intentional sprite overlap.
Add one compact mechanical cue, such as a blue forehead seam, side rivet, or square casing break, without adding noise.
